newsitem.title: THAILAND: Three Karen refugee camps raided, razed by fires.
newsitem.headline: Three Karen refugee camps raided, razed by fires.

text.p: Three Karen refugee camps housing nearly 36,000 people on the Thai-Burma border were set on fire and partially destroyed, Karen sources said on Wednesday.
A statement issued by the Karen National Union (KNU) said the three camps -- Hway Kaloke, Don Pa Kiang and Mae La -- were raided by unknown Burmese-speaking armed groups late on Tuesday night.
The camps are all just inside Thailand near Mae Sot in northwestern Thailand.
More than 70,000 Burmese refugees of Karen ethnic origin live in sprawling camps in Thailand. Many ethnic minorities have fled to Thailand to escape alleged human rights abuses by Burmese troops.
Citing one of the refugees who escaped Hway Kaloke, the KNU statement said about 100 men speaking Burmese entered the camp late at night, raided the market shops then set the camp on fire.
"A total of about 5,000 of the 6,729 people are homeless and destitute," the statement said.
Officials and relief workers were not immediately available for comment.
The KNU statement said there were reports of an ongoing battle between the invaders and camp residents at Mae La, which houses more than 25,000 residents.
"Reports from the Don Pa Kiang camp of 3,827 people indicate that the camp has been totally burned to the ground," it said.
Further details were not available, and Karen sources told Reuters they did not know if there were any casualties.
They said a clinic set up by Medecins sans Frontieres (Doctors Without Borders) at Hway Kaloke was ransacked and set on fire.
